TTF‑1 (nuclear) | Strong diffuse positivity | Supports pulmonary origin
CK7 (cytoplasmic) | Strong diffuse positivity | Consistent with adenocarcinoma

candidates.description: The histological subtype of the lung carcinoma as determined by pathology and immunohistochemistry.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Identify the diagnosis in the pathology report. Confirm the subtype using the Immunohistochemistry (IHC) table: look for p40/CK5/6 positivity for squamous and TTF-1/Napsin A/CK7 positivity for adenocarcinoma.
candidates.measurement_definition: Categorized as Squamous Cell Carcinoma if p40 or CK5/6 are positive and TTF-1/Napsin A are negative. Categorized as Adenocarcinoma if TTF-1 or Napsin A are positive and p40 is negative.
candidates.name: tumor_histology
candidates.uncertainty: Some reports may list 'non-small cell lung carcinoma' without specifying the subtype in the primary diagnosis line, necessitating reliance on IHC markers.

candidates.description: The percentage of tumor cells expressing the Ki-67 (MIB-1) proliferation marker.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Locate the Immunohistochemistry (IHC) section of the pathology report and extract the numeric percentage associated with the Ki-67 or MIB-1 marker.
candidates.measurement_definition: The percentage (%) of cells showing nuclear positivity for Ki-67 as reported in the IHC section of the pathology report.
candidates.name: ki67_labeling_index
candidates.uncertainty: The reports use the term 'Approximately', which introduces a small degree of measurement imprecision.

limitations: The available evidence is based on a small number of case reports.
IHC marker panels are not identical across all provided pathology reports.
summary: The evidence identifies distinct baseline histopathological and proliferative characteristics in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), specifically distinguishing between squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma via immunohistochemistry (IHC) and quantifying tumor proliferation via the Ki-67 labeling index.
